title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office has issued a decision outlining new guidelines for the development and use of AI systems. It emphasizes ethical standards, transparency, and adherence to regulatory requirements.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: This policy document announces an opening for a Technology Specialist in the AI office, outlining the role’s purpose and the types of AI projects they will support. It also describes the required technical skills, experience, and application steps for interested candidates.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The document announces a vacancy for the Lead Scientific Adviser position within the AI office. It outlines the responsibilities, qualifications, and application process for the role.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: This policy explains how an AI system can help legal officers identify and fill office vacancies, streamlining the hiring and staffing process. It also sets out rules for protecting data privacy, ensuring fair decisions, and keeping the AI’s actions transparent and accountable.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: This policy document addresses the need to fill vacancies for AI policy officers within the organization. It outlines the responsibilities, qualifications, and application process for these positions.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts set up to review and advise on the European Union’s proposed AI legislation, focusing on the technical and scientific aspects of the rules. They evaluate AI risks, recommend safeguards, and help shape the Act to ensure systems are safe, transparent, and compliant with EU standards.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The draft standardisation request proposes setting common guidelines and benchmarks for AI development and deployment to promote consistency and safety across the industry. It urges collaboration among stakeholders to define clear standards that will regulate AI technologies and encourage responsible innovation.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This notice informs stakeholders that the organization will hold a consultation to gather input on establishing a Community of Practice. It invites participants to share their perspectives and suggestions on the structure, goals, and implementation of this initiative.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document is an invitation for people to express their interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP). It outlines the simple steps for submitting an expression of interest and explains what will happen next with the applications.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The document presents a graphic that illustrates the iterative drafting process used by the Community of Practice (CoP). It shows how drafts are repeatedly reviewed, refined, and improved through cycles of feedback and revision until a final version is reached.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This document outlines the timeline of the drafting process for a Code of Practice, showing how the project evolved over time. It highlights key milestones, dates, and stages from the initial proposal through to final approval.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: The document is a first draft of a code of practice for AI, offering preliminary guidelines on how to use artificial intelligence responsibly. It sets out broad principles for safety, fairness, and transparency that organizations can adopt as they develop and deploy AI systems.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 2nd Draft provides a set of guidelines for organizations to implement responsible AI, covering aspects such as transparency, fairness, and accountability. It outlines best practices and compliance measures that help ensure AI systems are safe, reliable, and aligned with societal values.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: The document presents a set of guidelines and best practices for responsible AI use, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and accountability. It also defines roles and responsibilities for organizations, regulators, and developers, and includes mechanisms for monitoring compliance and updating the code as AI technology evolves.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a framework for responsible AI development and use. It outlines key principles such as transparency, fairness, and accountability, aiming to foster collaboration between stakeholders.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is an international agreement that commits signatory countries to develop and use artificial intelligence in a safe, ethical, and transparent manner. It establishes shared standards, accountability mechanisms, and collaborative research initiatives to ensure AI technologies benefit society while minimizing risks.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: These guidelines outline specific AI practices that are forbidden to prevent misuse and harm. They are designed to help organizations avoid unethical, illegal, or dangerous applications of artificial intelligence.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This policy explains what should be considered an AI system, outlining the key features and criteria that distinguish AI from other technologies. It helps organizations consistently identify, classify, and manage AI solutions for compliance and risk purposes.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines how to effectively communicate strategies that support start‑up growth and drive innovation within the organization. It emphasizes clear messaging, stakeholder engagement, and collaborative partnerships to build a vibrant ecosystem for new businesses.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a program that offers high‑performance computing resources and support to new tech companies across Europe. It aims to help start‑ups develop and scale AI and other data‑intensive projects by providing access to advanced HPC infrastructure, expertise, and potential funding opportunities.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This document explains how the organization will handle risks related to using AI, including how to spot potential problems and evaluate their severity. It also outlines steps to reduce or eliminate those risks, ensuring AI is used safely and responsibly.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar explores how to identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks associated with AI systems. It covers practical strategies for managing potential harms, ensuring safety, and maintaining responsible AI deployment.
